claims.claim: paired-eval has no third-party runtime dependencies and runs on the Python standard library from 3.9 up.
claims.metric: third-party runtime dependencies of the distributed package
claims.method: pyproject.toml declares dependencies = [] as a design constraint; requires-python is >=3.9

claims.claim: The 31 built-in tasks cannot detect a one-sided win rate below 25 percent, so they are a smoke set rather than a conclusive benchmark.
claims.metric: minimum detectable one-sided win rate (MDE) for 31 paired tasks at alpha 0.05 and 80 percent power
claims.method: detectable_effect runs a Monte-Carlo grid search whose decision rule is the same mcnemar_exact used by the tests (seed=0, 400 sims, step 0.01); docs/findings.md records approximately 0.24 for this call, the committed implementation returns 0.25 today, and the larger value is the one reported here

claims.claim: The mechanical mutation scan has 30 recorded surviving mutants, and any survivor beyond that baseline fails the pre-release check.
claims.metric: surviving mutants recorded in the mutation ratchet baseline
claims.method: mutate_auto.py mutates every mutation point and reruns the fast test suite as the oracle; checkall.sh stage 5 documents the full scan as 473 mutation points and compares survivors against mutation_baseline.json

check.note: counts the committed survivor list; the full `checkall.sh` ratchet (~25 minutes) is what regenerates it

claims.claim: On format-sensitive tasks a strict scaffold beat a bare instruction by 0.625 in pass rate, with every discordant pair favouring the scaffold.
claims.metric: scaffold main effect on pass rate in a 2x2 factorial over model and scaffold
claims.method: 4 format-sensitive tasks x 4 interleaved rounds; per-round McNemar exact with Holm correction gives p=0.0117 and discordant pairs 0:10; the effect reproduces across JSON object, JSON array, key=value and YAML, so it is not a single-task artifact
claims.repro: python3 -c "from paired_eval import reproduce_findings as r; r.check_scaffold_effect(call)"  # template: needs an injected model callable (see the reproduce_findings docstring); `python3 -m paired_eval.reproduce_findings` prints what it needs

check.manual: reproduce_findings needs an injected model callable (a real model call); the committed value is from the recorded run in docs/findings.md

claims.claim: Between the two models measured, the model main effect on these tasks is below 10 percent; this is a bounded null, not a demonstration of equality.
claims.metric: upper bound on the model main effect on pass rate
claims.method: 4 tasks x 20 rounds = 80 paired units at MDE 0.10 give delta=+0.025, CI95 [0.000, +0.075], discordant 5:3, p=0.727. This value supersedes an earlier over-claim (delta=0.000, p=1.000 on 16 units, whose MDE was 0.46 and could exclude almost nothing) retracted in docs/corrections.md
claims.repro: python3 -c "from paired_eval import reproduce_findings as r; r.check_model_null(call_a, call_b)"  # template: needs an injected model callable (see the reproduce_findings docstring); `python3 -m paired_eval.reproduce_findings` prints what it needs

check.manual: same: the 80-unit comparison needs a model; the recorded numbers and their CI live in docs/findings.md

claims.claim: Switching an agent from a single pass to draft-then-self-correct raised pass rate by 0.750 with the same model and the same bare instruction.
claims.metric: agent strategy effect on pass rate, single pass vs draft then self-correct
claims.method: same model, same bare instruction, one extra model call and no tools or prompt constraints added; CI95 [+0.250, +1.000], per-round McNemar p=0.00049, discordant pairs 12:0, concentration 0.33
claims.repro: python3 -c "from paired_eval import reproduce_findings as r; r.main(call, call_b=call_b, judge=judge)"  # template: needs an injected model callable (see the reproduce_findings docstring); `python3 -m paired_eval.reproduce_findings` prints what it needs

check.manual: needs a model call; see docs/findings.md for the recorded run

claims.claim: One clause of prompt wording moved the share of ungrounded claims from 0 percent to 86-89 percent, while the two models stayed indistinguishable.
claims.metric: share of claims in the final answer that no observation supports, under a must_ground trajectory policy
claims.method: same observations and same judge; under 'answer only from the source' all 8 claims were grounded, under 'add relevant background you know' 84 of 98 and 97 of 109 claims were ungrounded across 206 claims. The model-to-model comparison in the same experiment had only 4 paired prompts and is recorded as an uninformative null, so it is deliberately not claimed here
claims.repro: python3 -c "from paired_eval import reproduce_findings as r; r.main(call, call_b=call_b, judge=judge)"  # template: needs an injected model callable (see the reproduce_findings docstring); `python3 -m paired_eval.reproduce_findings` prints what it needs

check.manual: needs a model plus a judge; the 0% vs 86-89% split is from the recorded run in docs/findings.md

claims.claim: Self-check still adds 0.183 grounding rate on top of an already strict prompt, so scaffolding and self-check are diminishing but stackable rather than substitutes.
claims.metric: self-check increment in grounding rate when the strict prompt is already in place
claims.method: cross-item derivation tasks, the only screened family with headroom (reference cell 0.64-0.89): 18 paired units, CI95 [+0.086, +0.285], p=0.0046, independently reproduced on 18 fresh units at +0.281, p=0.0002. Two disclosed limits: this refutes an earlier 'either one is enough' reading whose 2x2 had both strict cells at the 1.000 ceiling, and the original n=18 sample-size argument was itself wrong (permutation power at n=18 is 0.45, required_pairs now returns 42), so the claim rests on the independent reproduction rather than on the first run
claims.repro: python3 -c "from paired_eval import reproduce_findings as r; r.check_derivation_increment(call, judge)"  # template: needs an injected model callable (see the reproduce_findings docstring); `python3 -m paired_eval.reproduce_findings` prints what it needs

check.manual: needs a model plus a judge; recorded in docs/findings.md

claims.claim: The model-dependent figures this file marks manual are the same numbers `docs/findings.md` records — the two published copies of that run cannot drift apart.
claims.value: every manual figure appears in docs/findings.md
claims.metric: each manual claim's published number, looked up in docs/findings.md
claims.method: reads the claims marked manual, extracts the numbers each one publishes, and requires every one of them to appear in docs/findings.md. This proves the gate's copy and the document's copy agree; it does NOT prove the run happened. The per-item outputs behind those figures were never committed, which is exactly why those claims stay manual.
claims.repro: python3 -m verify_claims --root . list | grep manual; grep -nE '0\.625|0\.750|0\.183|0\.10' docs/findings.md

check.cmd: python3 -c "import json,re,pathlib;d=json.loads(pathlib.Path('docs/claims.json').read_text(encoding='utf-8'));doc=pathlib.Path('docs/findings.md').read_text(encoding='utf-8');man=[c for c in d['claims'] if 'manual' in (c.get('check') or {})];toks=[t for c in man for t in re.findall(r'\d+(?:\.\d+)?', str(c.get('value')))];toks=[t for t in toks if '.' in t or len(t)>=2];missing=[t for t in toks if t not in doc];print('figures', len(toks), 'missing', missing);assert not missing, missing"
